bibl.title: An emergent population code in primary auditory cortex supports selective attention to spectral and temporal sound features

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Rather, these results suggest that sound-encoding in A1 relies on synergies among neurons, and these synergies support the neural code for selective listening.

span.label: feature-selective auditory attention
span.quote: In order to illuminate how A1 supports flexible perception in rich acoustic environments, we recorded from A1 neurons while rhesus macaques performed a feature-selective attention task.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: We recorded from 92 A1 neurons of two adult rhesus macaques, one female (W, 8 kg) and one male (U, 12 kg).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because feature tuning co-varies within single neurons, a gain applied to individual cells cannot separate the two features; only re-weighting neurons at the population level recovers a feature-specific signal.
span.quote: In other words, A1 neurons rarely uniquely encode one sound feature or the other because feature tuning co-varies at the single-neuron level (similar to Fig. 3e-h). This prevents single-neuron tuning from providing a robust basis for attentional perceptual enhancement.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Mixed selectivity cancels the average effect of feature-specific gain, which is why single-neuron measures show nothing while the population does.
span.quote: Thus, when single neurons exhibit mixed selectivity in their tuning to different sensory features, FSG as a mechanism of attention exhibits no average attentional enhancement (Fig. 3g,h).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The attentional benefit is carried by higher-order correlations among neurons, i.e. it is an emergent property of the ensemble rather than a sum of single-cell effects.
span.quote: This suggests that our observed population enhancement of sound feature encoding constitutes an emergent effect, relying on higher-order correlations among A1 neurons.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Population coding unfolds in stages over the stimulus: a fast feature-general change detection followed by finer feature discrimination.
span.quote: These temporal dynamics suggest that early population responses function to detect a rapid change, irrespective of feature, whereas sustained responses elicit finer-grained feature selectivity.

span.label: The analysis uses only firing rate, not spike timing.
span.quote: An important consideration of the present report is our exclusive use of firing rate, as opposed to spike-timing measures of neural activity.

span.label: Because many bandwidth targets were also amplitude-modulated, phase locking could signal a target in both attention conditions, so the task may not have been demanding enough to reveal attentional effects on spike timing.
span.quote: It is important to note that the design of our task is such that, even when attending to the spectral feature, many target sounds are temporally modulated as well, and therefore phase-locking can signal the presence of a target in both attention conditions.

span.label: Neurons were pooled across sessions and trials resampled, so real correlated and intrinsic variability had to be reintroduced by modelling rather than measured simultaneously.
span.quote: An important consideration with this approach is that, by combining neurons across experimental sessions, and by randomly re-sampling trials, we fail to approximate correlated and intrinsic variability between and within neurons, respectively.

span.label: The task may be too easy to force attention-related changes in A1 temporal dynamics.
span.quote: Thus, the present task may not sufficiently challenge the auditory system to drive attention-related changes in the temporal dynamics of A1 neurons’ spiking.

span.label: The two levels of analysis disagree on the same data: attention does not enhance the single-neuron representation, while the population analysis shows enhanced encoding.
span.quote: attention does not enhance the single-neuron representation of attended features in our data. However, a population-level analysis reveals that ensembles of neurons exhibit enhanced encoding of attended sound features, and this population code tracks subjects’ performance.

span.label: The physical stimulus differs between animals, because the values were tailored to each subject's own psychophysical thresholds rather than fixed.
span.quote: The precise AM and ∆BW values used during recording sessions were tailored to each subject’s psychophysical thresholds for detection of each sound feature (AM and ∆BW) in isolation, determined prior to recording.

span.label: The condition labels are defined by a sensitivity criterion, not by a physical quantity: 'near threshold' means the level at which d-prime equals 1.
span.quote: Three values of each feature were used in recording sessions: one near psychophysical threshold (defined as the modulation level at which the subject’s sensitivity, measured using d’ (Wickens, 2002) was equal to 1), one slightly above threshold (d’ ~ 1.2), and one well above threshold (d’> 1.5).

span.label: An inclusion decision was made and checked, and the check is reported rather than the criterion being justified in advance.
span.quote: Removing SUs with only 2 experimental blocks of isolation (n = 58) from analysis does not qualitatively affect our results nor main conclusions and interpretations.

span.label: the AM frequency presented on each trial chosen AT RANDOM rather than adaptively
span.quote: We chose to randomly select the presented AM frequency to avoid biasing our recordings toward AM-sensitive neurons

span.label: sensory representation - AT THE SINGLE-NEURON LEVEL: not enhanced by attention in these data, which is the paper's own negative result
span.quote: attention does not enhance the single-neuron representation of attended features in our data.

span.label: sensory representation - AT THE POPULATION LEVEL: enhanced, tracking behaviour, and described as an emergent code NOT MEASURABLE at the single-neuron level
span.quote: These results suggest that an emergent population code not measurable at the single-neuron level might constitute the functional unit of sensory representation in PSC.

span.label: psychophysical threshold - defined as the modulation level at which the subject's measured d-prime equals 1, so the condition is fixed by sensitivity rather than by the stimulus
span.quote: one near psychophysical threshold (defined as the modulation level at which the subject’s sensitivity, measured using d’ (Wickens, 2002) was equal to 1)

span.label: contradicts → Niwa et al. (2012b), Schwartz and David (2017) and von Trapp et al. (2016), which reported attention-related changes in A1 single-neuron tuning
span.quote: Therefore, when comparing feature tuning across the more rigorous demands of different feature attention conditions, we do not observe tuning changes that have been found in several prior studies comparing A1 tuning between passive vs. active conditions and between attend-toward vs. attend-away conditions (Niwa et al., 2012b; Schwartz and David, 2017; von Trapp et al., 2016).

span.label: builds-on → Mante et al. (2013) and Rigotti et al. (2013) population-level analyses of prefrontal cortex
span.quote: This prompted us to conduct a population-level analysis, inspired by studies performed in PFC (Mante et al., 2013; Rigotti et al., 2013), to make sense of the heterogeneous single-neuron representations.

span.label: single-neuron representation —contrasted-with→ population code
span.quote: attention does not enhance the single-neuron representation of attended features in our data. However, a population-level analysis reveals that ensembles of neurons exhibit enhanced encoding of attended sound features, and this population code tracks subjects’ performance.

span.label: logistic regression
span.quote: The coefficients are derived from the following binomial logistic regression model:

span.label: multiple linear regression
span.quote: We quantified encoding of behavioral (context) and acoustic (AM and BW) variables on the firing rates of recorded A1 neurons (n = 92) using multiple linear regression (Equation 2).

span.label: Wilcoxon signed rank test
span.quote: Statistical significance was determined within each monkey using a sign rank test comparing each feature’s behavioral coefficient between attention conditions (p was <0.001 for each of the 4 tests).

span.label: ROC / signal detection analysis
span.quote: We also calculated the area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC area)

span.label: bootstrap
span.quote: Since many of our neurons were recorded during different sessions, we used a bootstrapping approach to estimate the mean and variance of population projections.

span.label: Spearman correlation
span.quote: measured by the sign of the coefficient (Spearman correlation, r = 0.37, p < 0.001).

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Each significance test was a single-distribution t-test with a null hypothesis of CP=0.5.

span.label: support vector machine with held-out test set
span.term: support vector machine with held-out test set
span.quote: A linear support vector machine was fit to a training set and performance evaluated on a test set of withheld data.

span.label: Fano factor (variance-to-mean ratio)
span.quote: We determined the desired neuronintrinsic variability by calculating the Fano factor (variance/mean rate) for each neuron and scaling its simulated spike count distribution to match the observed Fano factor.

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: Contributions of SUs to the signal were determined offline using k-means and principal component analysis-based spike sorting software in Spike2 (CED).

span.label: z-score standardisation
span.quote: by z-scoring spike count distributions across stimuli and task context

span.label: linear regression
span.quote: pairs of neurons in the data (n = 434 pairs) and fitting a linear regression to those noise

span.label: Individual A1 neurons carried mixed selectivity, encoding both the spectral and temporal sound features and the attention condition.
span.quote: We find that single neurons tend to be highdimensional, in that they exhibit substantial mixed selectivity for both sound features, as well as task context.

span.label: Attention produced no average enhancement of feature encoding in single A1 neurons.
span.quote: Contrary to common findings in many previous experiments, attention does not enhance the single-neuron representation of attended features in our data.

span.label: Single-neuron feature sensitivity measured by ROC area was statistically identical across the two attention conditions.
span.quote: Though we do observe some scatter around the unity line, neurons increase or decrease their AM ROC area with equal likelihood, (sign rank test, p = 0.74).

span.label: Attention was the variable with a significant main effect in the largest number of neurons, yet interactions with feature tuning were rare.
span.quote: Context had a significant main effect in more neurons than either acoustic feature, as measured by the proportion of neurons with significant context coefficients

span.label: AM and bandwidth tuning were positively correlated across neurons, so a single neuron's rate cannot disambiguate which feature changed.
span.quote: measured by the sign of the coefficient (Spearman correlation, r = 0.37, p < 0.001).

span.label: After targeted dimensionality reduction, the population code decoded each sound feature better when that feature was attended.
span.quote: However, a population-level analysis reveals that ensembles of neurons exhibit enhanced encoding of attended sound features, and this population code tracks subjects’ performance.

span.label: The attentional advantage in the population code was large and highly reliable across simulated populations.
span.quote: Across 100 simulated neural populations, the average ROC enhancement is 0.151 for AM (p=2.41e-30)

span.label: The observed attentional modulation exceeded that of every surrogate population in which higher-order correlations had been destroyed.
span.quote: Comparing the attentional modulation index (z-score of ROC difference of attended relative to unattended feature) of the neural data (9c, vertical red line) to that of 1000 surrogate populations, we find no overlap between our observed attentional enhancement and that expected by the simpler single-neuron and pairwise covariance properties.

span.label: Trial-by-trial population projections predicted whether the animal answered correctly, along each task-variable axis.
span.quote: The distribution of choice probability (CP) values across 100 simulated populations reveals a significant relationship between AM-axis projections and task performance, as evidenced by a mean CP across simulations of 0.573 (p=1.90e-39).

span.label: Both monkeys weighted the attended feature more heavily than the unattended one in their yes/no reports.
span.quote: Each subject performed the task above chance, as evidenced by a greater influence of the attended feature vs. the unattended feature on the probability of a “Yes” response (Figure 2; 47 total sessions, p = 8.98e-8 ; sign rank test, collapsed across monkeys).

span.label: Attention did not alter spike timing: phase locking to the temporal envelope was unaffected by the attention condition.
span.quote: However, we find no evidence of attention-related effects on phase locking (Figure 11), suggesting that phase-locking may not be relevant for feature-selective attention in the context of this task in A1.

span.label: Population subspace trajectories were initially feature-ambiguous and only separated by feature partway through the stimulus.
span.quote: Trajectories in both conditions exhibit an early, non-selective course wherein each stimulus projects to roughly the same area within the subspace.

span.label: targeted dimensionality reduction (TDR)
span.quote: TDR is a method of calculating a weighted average of neural activity across a sample of neurons.

span.label: de-mixing by TDR
span.quote: TDR both reduces the dimensionality of the population response from # neurons to # projections and provides a way of “de-mixing” neural activity across a population of neurons with mixed selectivity.

span.label: feature-specific gain (FSG)
span.quote: whereby the response of a neuron is determined by both its sensory response function and a multiplicative gain parameter that depends on the neuron’s preference for the attended feature, yielding larger responses when attention is directed toward the neuron’s preferred feature.

span.label: ROC area as a neural sensitivity measure
span.term: ROC area as a neural sensitivity measure
span.quote: If a neuron’s ROC area is 0.5, that is interpreted as a failure to detect the presence of a feature.

span.label: choice probability (CP)
span.quote: In order to quantify these effects, we calculated the ROC area between correct and incorrect response distributions, a metric commonly referred to as “Choice Probability” (CP) (Britten et al., 1992).

span.label: conditions versus variables in this study
span.term: conditions versus variables in this study
span.quote: We refer to “variables” as the three dimensions along which all conditions vary, namely the two sound features (AM, ∆BW) and context (attention).

span.label: surrogate population
span.quote: This method constructs surrogate populations by shuffling the original data labels, but then recovering (to the extent possible) the marginal and covariance features of the original data by transforming the shuffled data using a “readout” matrix.

span.label: attended feature / task context (Attend AM versus Attend BW block)
span.term: attended feature / task context (Attend AM versus Attend BW block)
span.quote: Context was coded as a binary factor (-1 or 1 for Attend BW and Attend AM, respectively).

span.label: amplitude modulation depth of the second sound
span.term: amplitude modulation depth of the second sound
span.quote: AM depth values were 28, 40, and 100% for monkey U and 40, 60, and 100% for monkey W.

span.label: spectral bandwidth change of the second sound
span.term: spectral bandwidth change of the second sound
span.quote: Experimental values of ∆BW were 0.375, 0.5, and 1 octave for monkey U and 0.5, 0.75, and 1.5 octaves for monkey W.

span.label: trial-by-trial spike count over the 400 ms stimulus
span.term: trial-by-trial spike count over the 400 ms stimulus
span.quote: We analyzed the effects of task context, AM and ∆BW on spike counts calculated over the entirety of each 400-ms stimulus.

span.label: the monkey's yes/no behavioural report
span.quote: Subjects then used the joystick to make a behavioral report, a “Yes” or “No” response indicating whether they detected the attended sound feature in S2.

span.label: AM frequency, randomised across sessions to avoid sampling bias
span.term: AM frequency, randomised across sessions to avoid sampling bias
span.quote: We chose to randomly select the presented AM frequency to avoid biasing our recordings toward AM-sensitive neurons at the expense of sampling from ∆BW-sensitive neurons.

span.label: noise correlations and neuron-intrinsic variability imposed on the simulated populations
span.term: noise correlations and neuron-intrinsic variability imposed on the simulated populations
span.quote: Therefore, the matrix of simulated spike counts within a condition is transformed to introduce noise correlations and neuron-intrinsic variability that match that observed in the data.

span.label: feature levels set to each subject's own psychophysical threshold
span.term: feature levels set to each subject's own psychophysical threshold
span.quote: The precise AM and ∆BW values used during recording sessions were tailored to each subject’s psychophysical thresholds for detection of each sound feature (AM and ∆BW) in isolation, determined prior to recording.

span.label: 92 — single A1 neurons recorded, from two rhesus macaques
span.quote: We recorded from 92 A1 neurons of two adult rhesus macaques, one female (W, 8 kg) and one male (U, 12 kg).

span.label: 0.151 — average increase in population ROC area for AM when AM was the attended feature
span.quote: Across 100 simulated neural populations, the average ROC enhancement is 0.151 for AM (p=2.41e-30)

span.label: p = 0.73 and 0.74 — sign rank p-values showing no attentional change in single-neuron BW and AM sensitivity
span.quote: AM ROC and BW ROC distributions each lie along the unity line, indicating no average effect of attention (p = 0.73 and 0.74, respectively).

span.label: 0.633 (p=1.12e-61) — mean choice probability for projections into the full three-dimensional task-variable subspace
span.quote: values across simulated populations lying above 0.5, with a mean of 0.633 (p=1.12e-61).

span.label: 1000 — surrogate populations built with intact single-neuron tuning but destroyed higher-order correlations
span.quote: we constructed 1000 “surrogate” populations with intact single-neuron tuning but decimated higherorder correlations among them (Elsayed and Cunningham, 2017).

span.label: 26 (13 x 2) — total experimental conditions, being 13 sound combinations crossed with two attention blocks
span.quote: have 26 total experimental conditions (13 AM*∆BW combinations across two attention conditions).

span.label: 47 total sessions, p = 8.98e-8 — behavioural sessions and the sign rank p-value showing attention shifted the animals' feature weighting
span.quote: (Figure 2; 47 total sessions, p = 8.98e-8 ; sign rank test, collapsed across monkeys).

span.label: n = 434 pairs — simultaneously recorded neuron pairs used to estimate the noise correlations imposed on simulated populations
span.quote: pairs of neurons in the data (n = 434 pairs) and fitting a linear regression to those noise

span.label: 65 dB SPL — calibrated presentation level of every sound stimulus at the outer ear
span.quote: Each stimulus was calibrated to an intensity of 65 dB SPL at the outer ear (A-weighted; Bruel & Kjaer model 2231).

span.label: 400 ms — duration of each of the two sounds in a trial
span.quote: Sounds were 400 ms in duration with 5-ms cosine ramps at onset and offset.
